definition: DSPy lets you program LLMs with typed modules instead of hand-written prompts, then automatically optimises the prompts and examples.
details: Created by Omar Khattab and colleagues at Stanford NLP (2023); now developed by an open-source community with Databricks contributions.

explainer.lead: How to install DSPy, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
import dspy

dspy.configure(lm=dspy.LM("openai/gpt-4o-mini"))

classify = dspy.Predict("sentence -> sentiment: bool")
print(classify(sentence="The new release is fantastic.").sentiment)

qa = dspy.ChainOfThought("question -> answer")
print(qa(question="Why do transformers use positional encodings?").answer)

explainer.inAi: Write the pipeline once, then let an optimiser such as MIPROv2 tune prompts against your metric and a few labelled examples.
explainer.jsNote: DSPy is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.
